name: Hydrogen refuelling stations
principle: Stations take delivered or on-site hydrogen, compress and cool it, and dispense it at 350 or 700 bar to fuel cell vehicles. IEA counted about 1,300 stations at the end of 2024, 15% more than 2023. China had more than 500 (up 30%) and Europe more than 300. Station counts fell in the US, and Austria's only operator, OMV, announced closure of all stations by September 2025.

performance.metric: hydrogen refuelling stations worldwide at end 2024

source.note: IEA Global Hydrogen Review 2025 (collected in corpus/iea-reports): hydrogen refuelling stations

costs.metric: station capital equipment cost per unit dispensing capacity
costs.basis: 111 new fueling stations awarded by the California Energy Commission in 2020; capacity 770-1,620 kg/day, all 700-bar light-duty; uninstalled equipment capital cost (combined awarded grant and match funding), adjusted to 2016 dollars using Chemical Engineering Plant Cost Indices; equivalent to USD 300-890/(kg/day) per dispenser

source.note: DOE Hydrogen Program Record 21002, Hydrogen Fueling Station Capital Cost, 11 February 2021

costs.basis: mean and median total capital cost across the 111 California-awarded stations; average capacity 1,240 kg/day, median 1,500 kg/day; uninstalled equipment capital cost in 2016 dollars

source.note: DOE Hydrogen Program Record 21002, Hydrogen Fueling Station Capital Cost, 11 February 2021

limitations: Reliability and hydrogen supply problems closed stations in US and Austria
